title: A minimal component attains the dimension maximum
statement: Let k be a field and S a commutative finite type k-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let p be a prime ideal and d,r natural numbers with dim(S_p)=d [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime; def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and trdeg_k(kappa(p))=r [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. There exists a minimal prime q of S contained in p with dim(S/q)=d+r.

proof.text: localization prime correspondence identifies the lengths of chains below p with those in S_p. Since hd is the finite natural number d, the supremum of these lengths is attained: if no chain had length d, all lengths would be at most d-1 (and for d=0 the single-prime chain already attains it). A length-d chain below p ends at p and starts at a minimal prime q of S; otherwise appending p or prepending a smaller prime would contradict the bound d. It is saturated for the same reason. Ideal correspondence gives a saturated chain from zero to the image of p in the finite type domain S/q. The residue field of p is the fraction field of S/p. The finite type domain dimension/transcendence-degree theorem and hr give dim(S/p) = r, and the maximal-chain theorem supplies a saturated chain of length r above p ending at a maximal ideal. Append this to the length-d chain, counting p only once. It is a maximal chain in S/q. The domain maximal-chain theorem makes its length d+r equal to dim(S/q), giving the required q, its primality and minimality.
